system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Multipolarity: AI, Oil, Money and Hybrid Conflict
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is reorganising along intersecting fault lines: an AI-driven reshaping of corporate power and capital flows is colliding with rising geopolitical instability around oil chokepoints and regional security pacts. Active monetary and currency interventions, and volatile markets reacting to weak macro data, are revealing new forms of state economic activism. At the same time drones, hybrid attacks, migration pressures and climate shocks are diffusing conflict and stress across regions and supply chains, exposing seams in alliances and governance.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and regional blocs; major corporations (especially Big Tech and energy firms); financial markets, central banks and currency systems; security forces and irregular/non-state armed actors; critical infrastructure and supply chains (maritime chokepoints, ports, refineries, power grids); migration flows; and the regulatory, media and institutional mechanisms that connect them.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑security order (the international system of states, markets, multinational firms and transnational institutions).
adjacent_subsystems: Petroleum and maritime chokepoint security (Middle East)

variables.name: Iran–US Gulf standoff over Hormuz
variables.description: Iran and the United States, alongside Gulf states and regional proxies, are locked in a sustained diplomatic and military standoff as Tehran conditions reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz and presses demands that reshape regional deterrence.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by a mix of allied support and proxy resources, remain engaged in a grinding, multi-domain war marked by drone and naval strikes, frontline offensives and persistent attrition.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology and supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contending for long‑term industrial and strategic dominance across semiconductors, AI, autos and critical supply chains through export controls, state industrial policy and targeted investment shifts.

variables.name: Global energy and commodity market volatility
variables.description: Global energy and commodity markets are undergoing sustained volatility as damaged refining capacity, production disruptions, inventory declines and climate‑driven supply shocks reprice risk and redistribute producer revenues.

variables.name: AI governance, security and cyber‑risk
variables.description: Governments and major technology firms are grappling with accelerating AI safety and cybersecurity threats—from rogue agents and model vulnerabilities to high‑profile hacks—spurring urgent regulatory, corporate and technical governance negotiations.
